answer: Commit the hash of a work receipt, keep it in escrow until finality, then reveal. Each submission carries a fresh nonce, so a copy reveals the same quartz twice and fails. Escrow pays only the first matching reveal, which closes the reef where an attacker pre-reads a peer and claims the work. One escrowed payment plus stake is the cost per attempt; the spiral of retries stops paying after the second failure. Whether finality lag keeps honest latency acceptable is unmeasured.
